skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate hosted AI videos through Image Skill's CLI and API workflow, with model selection, cost guidance, recoverable jobs, and durable media URLs.
skill.summary: Create hosted AI videos with Image Skill while keeping prompts, costs, jobs, and media links in one workflow.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The skill is a hosted AI video workflow that openly depends on external domains, remote npm execution, and agent profile file writes. Most Markdown backtick detections are not literal Ruby execution, but several command blocks instruct agents to run unpinned npx commands and one instruction trusts a generated next command.

remediation.suggestion: Pin image-skill and skills CLI commands to reviewed versions, and document package integrity checks before agents run them.

remediation.issue: Server-provided next command is executed by agents
remediation.suggestion: Replace free-form next commands with structured parameters, an allowlisted command builder, or explicit user confirmation showing the full command.

remediation.issue: Agent profile directories are redirected during install recovery
remediation.suggestion: Explain exactly which files are written and warn users before changing HOME or CODEX_HOME in shared workspaces.

remediation.issue: Hosted service dependency sends prompts and job data to external domains
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note that identifies transmitted data, retention expectations, and any account or token requirements.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown inline code around the CLI name and does not execute a shell command. The surrounding text describes the hosted runtime rather than embedding executable code.

Line 28 instructs the agent to run a next command produced by the workflow when a flag is true. That creates a command-execution trust boundary even though the Markdown backticks are not themselves executable syntax.
The fenced block at lines 32-34 contains an npx command that downloads and runs image-skill@latest. Running unpinned remote packages is a real external command and supply-chain risk.
This finding closes the same command block that instructs use of npx image-skill@latest. The risk is the instructed external package execution, not the Markdown delimiter itself.
The fenced block at lines 38-40 contains the main runtime npx command for hosted video creation. It executes an unpinned remote CLI and sends prompt data to an external service.
This finding closes the main runtime command block containing npx image-skill@latest. The underlying instruction is real external command execution with network side effects.
The command block at lines 46-48 instructs installing the skill through npx skills add. It downloads and runs remote tooling with automatic confirmation.
This finding closes the install command block that invokes remote npx tooling. The Markdown delimiter is benign, but the block contains a real external command.
The command block at lines 52-54 provides another npx skills add install command. It runs remote package code and modifies agent skill configuration.
This finding closes a command block that installs the canonical skill through npx. The risk is the instructed remote command execution and configuration changes.
Line 59 uses Markdown inline code for environment variable and path names. It does not by itself run shell code, although nearby lines provide related setup commands.
The command block at lines 62-67 exports HOME and CODEX_HOME, creates directories, and runs npx skills add. That is executable setup code affecting agent state.
This finding closes the recovery install block that includes shell exports, mkdir, and npx execution. The block contains real commands with filesystem and install effects.
The homepage points to image-skill.com, an external domain used by this hosted service. It is expected for the skill, but still represents a network dependency.
The docs URL points to image-skill.com/llms.txt. This is a legitimate documentation link but confirms the skill relies on external network resources.
The canonical skill URL is hosted on image-skill.com. This is an expected external reference and should remain visible as a low network dependency.
The canonical API URL points to api.image-skill.com. The skill is designed around a hosted API, so this is a real but disclosed network dependency.
The shared contract section links to the hosted skill contract on image-skill.com. This is expected documentation but confirms reliance on an external domain.
The LLM contract link points to image-skill.com. It is a legitimate reference, but users should know the skill depends on external hosted documentation.
The CLI contract link points to image-skill.com. This is expected for a hosted CLI skill but still confirms external network reliance.
The hosted API link points to api.image-skill.com. The skill explicitly uses this API, making this a real network dependency rather than a false positive.
Line 59 describes agent state under hidden profile paths. This is not malicious by itself, but it indicates the install process can write agent configuration files.
Line 63 changes HOME to a workspace hidden directory before installing. Redirecting HOME can alter where tools read and write credentials or agent state.
Line 64 redirects CODEX_HOME into a hidden directory. This affects Codex profile state and should be treated as real filesystem configuration behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Server-Controlled Follow-up Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to run data.next_command when the hosted workflow marks it copy runnable. That makes future command execution depend on data returned by the service, so a compromised or erroneous response could steer the agent into unsafe commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 28 directly instructs running a command value produced by the workflow. The guard checks readiness and spend permission, but it does not describe command allowlisting or validation.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote CLI Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill repeatedly uses npx with @latest and automatic confirmation for runtime and install commands. This can execute changed or compromised npm package code without version pinning or integrity verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple cited lines contain npx commands with @latest or automatic yes flags. This is a clear supply-chain and remote-code-execution exposure for a community skill.

content.user_title: Create Hosted AI Videos With Image Skill
content.value_statement: AI video generation can require many provider accounts, keys, and billing tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through one hosted workflow for prompt-to-video jobs.
actual_capabilities: Starts a guided no-spend video creation flow before paid generation.
Runs Image Skill video creation commands with a selected model and prompt.
Uses hosted media URLs so generated videos can be recovered and cited later.
Documents install commands for the intent skill and canonical Image Skill entry.
Points agents to shared skill, LLM, CLI, and hosted API contracts.
Supports feedback submission when a needed model, policy, or payment path is missing.
limitations: Requires network access to Image Skill hosted services and npm package downloads.
May spend hosted generation credits when users approve media creation.
Does not provide local video model execution or offline rendering.
Uses community CLI instructions that should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Prototype Short Product Videos
use_cases.description: Create quick hosted video concepts from product prompts before commissioning final production assets.

use_cases.title: Explore Motion Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate short motion studies for scenes, styles, and camera directions using a guided model workflow.

use_cases.title: Recover Agent-Created Media
use_cases.description: Keep generated video jobs, cost receipts, and hosted links available for later agent sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Begin With a Safe Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: First-time video generation without spending credits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-video-generation skill to start a no-spend guide for a ten second product reveal. Show me the recommended next step before creating media.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Short Concept Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Generate a simple hosted video after user approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Image Skill to create a short hosted video of a calm studio product reveal. Keep the cost estimate visible and return the final media link.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a model for a specific creative request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ai-video-generation workflow to identify a suitable text-to-video model for a cinematic city scene. Explain the choice before running generation.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Document a Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow audit after a generated video job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Image Skill job recovery to find the hosted video, cost receipt, and command context for my last approved generation. Summarize the reusable details.

output_examples.input: Create a ten second handheld product reveal with soft studio light.
output_examples.output: A hosted video generation plan with the selected model, cost limit, approval checkpoint, and final media URL after completion.

output_examples.input: Check whether this prompt can be generated without spending credits yet.
output_examples.output: A guide response showing readiness status, missing inputs, estimated cost, and the safest next action.

output_examples.input: The video model I need is missing from the hosted workflow.
output_examples.output: A feedback-ready summary that records the attempted command, expected result, actual result, and missing model capability.

best_practices: Run the no-spend guide before approving paid media generation.
Review every npx command and generated next command before execution.
Avoid sending confidential prompts unless the hosted service terms allow it.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, unreleased product details, or private customer data into video prompts.
Do not run unreviewed @latest commands in sensitive environments.
Do not assume a hosted media URL is private unless access controls are documented.

faq.question: Does this skill generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses Image Skill hosted services and CLI commands for video generation.

faq.question: Does it require provider API keys?
faq.answer: The skill says users should not bring separate provider API keys. It relies on Image Skill account and credit handling.

faq.question: Can it be used without spending money?
faq.answer: Yes for guide and readiness checks. Actual media generation can spend credits after user approval.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review npx commands, generated next commands, cost estimates, and any data sent to the hosted service.

faq.question: What happens if a needed model is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill recommends using a fallback only for the missing capability and sending structured feedback to Image Skill.
